text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and Queen Noor return home after a private visit to a number of European countries.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says Jordan "aspires to a future when peace prevails and the voices of aggression and cries of expansionism recede."
- Head of Arab League arrives in Amman on Sunday on a three-day visit to attend meeting of Arab businessmen.
- Ex-governor of Jordan Central Bank says in a public lecture that Jordan succeeded in reducing its debt burden and overall servicing of its interest.
- Prime Minister says government's programme for the next five years is a "social and developmental one" based on getting closer to a self-sufficient economy.
- Opposition meetings step up calls on Jordanians to stage a sit-in in front of planned Israeli trade fair this week.
- A government move to downsize municipalities across Jordan to 50 from an existing 291 bodies due to financial problems many face, Kabariti says.
- Ex-governor of central bank urges the government to continue to fix the dinar's exchange rate to ensure monetary stability.

- Government to start implementing multi-million dollar "social safety net" programmes to help ease widespread poverty and unemployment by mid-1997, say officials. It includes a fund to finance projects for small and medium sized enterprises and a job creation fund for the poor.
- UNRWA (United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees) employees threaten strike action over pay demands.
- Jordan is confident of the future, Kabariti tells Ajloun residents.
- Delegation headed by trade and industry minister tentatively scheduled to leave for Baghdad on Wednesday, two days later than originally planned, official sources say.
